Awesome 3-player co-op 3rd person squad shooter/wave survival game, with the following caveats:

- No host migration. If the host goes down and ragequits, everyone loses their progress. If the host is lagging and drops, everyone loses their progress.
- No in-game communication beyond waypoint pings and emotes. No text chat, no voice chat. You will need to use a third-party
- No ability to join/rejoin mid-mission.

Those issues aside (and to be honest, they're fairly minor issues), I'm having a great time with this title. I got it on sale and was half expecting to refund after an hour or so, but most of the progression seems horizontal and there's a lot of build flexibility. Weapon/attachment unlocks are never exclusive to one class, so you're rewarded for experimenting - what doesn't work in one situation might work in another, or on another class. Everything seems to have its place. You're also encouraged to make liberal use of gameplay mutators - each mission, all 3 players can offer a challenge card (one is selected at random and the other two returned to their owners), offering greater rewards for completing the mission while the challenge is active.

Looking forward to unlocking the horde mode/area defense game modes, harder difficulties, and whatever "hardcore campaign" is.

It's hard not to recommend for an Aliens fan. This current all time low sale price of $20 for the base and pathogen expansion feels perfect. $30 isn't terrible for the base, but $15 for Pathogen is a bit much, so definitely catch that on sale if you miss this one.
The story is surprisingly good, again if you're into Aliens. Voice work is great. How the campaign actually unfolds a story is great and akin to L4D or Vermintide 2, but you actually have to play it in order, so it's coherent.
The game itself has some jank and strange decisions, but it gets the important bits right.
The 7 different classes (kits) all feel good and distinct with different roles for a fireteam. The customization within kits is also plentiful to cater to your tastes with the perk and modifier grid system.
Gunplay is good. Smart guns feels fantastic and powerful on a horde like you'd think from the movies. Tons of weapons and attachments to choose from, both bought from a store and found/unlocked.
There are consumable items like mines, turrets, and force fields that you can use to entrench positions.
After you play the campaign, you unlock alternate game modes consisting of several different maps with different spice like xeno horde waves, so you don't only have the option of repeating the campaign endlessly. 
Downsides: No in-game communication like text or voice chat, just emotes and a non-contextual ping, truly a strange choice for a modern game. Low player count, but there is crossplay with Xbox and PS, so its not ridiculous to matchmake, especially on the later difficulties and post-campaign gamemodes (the discord is pretty active as well). Peer to peer with no ping display, so bad hosts can lag, drop, and burn a run since there's no reconnecting (or mid-run join either).
I've not stuck with many a horde shooter before due to boredom of some variety (too repetitive, poor combat, bad/no progression, etc.) but AFE has a satisfying loop that outweighs the downsides in my book. It really feels like playing as a colonial marine a la Aliens, and who (again, of aliens fans) wouldn't enjoy that?
Got it gifted to me from a friend. Story is short. Would like more story. Just kinda left it after i finished the story. Other than that, its a game. Good game on sale though. Would still recommend.

What is Aliens:Fireteam Elite?

Its basicly a PvE hordeshooter. You and 2 Friends or AI partners run from point A to point B and shoot aliens while doing so. Reaching Point B you allways have to defend against a Horde of Enemies for a certain amount of time or amount of Enemies. After doing so, you continue this gameplay loop until the level end is reached. While that sounds somewhat very basic and dull, I found it actually very enjoyable. The Game is filled to the brim with Fanservice and little details I absolutely loved.

I am a Kid of the 90´s. Ellen Ripley was a strong Female main protagonist way before all that woke nonsense. The Movie Aliens is one of my most beloved movies of all time. And for people like me, who absolutely adore the Franchise this is a real gift.

The Sound of the Pulse Rifle, the Smartgun, the way the aliens claw around them while you blast them to pieces. I absolutely Love it! And all the little details show, how much the developer cared for this game. While doing your missions, you allways got your Operator connected. "Herrera" a latin american though women and a Scientist that you rescue early on. The Dialogues between those two are often just awesome and very memoreable. Also Randomized somewhat, so that you dont hear the same voicelines everytime. That alone showed me, how much this is Fanservice. I wont go into detail here to much for the sake of Spoilers.


To keep you entertained while playing, every mission has a hidden cache somewhere so there is a Ton of weapons, decals, colours, emotes and all that stuff to collect for you. There is also a Levelsystem in place with perks and different combinations of those to fiddle around with.

I Bought this game discounted, even tho I actually love it, but I dont think its worth 40€. Mostly because im a cheap guy and know the next steam sale will come. 20€ Is money well spent on this. I did have alot of Fun and intent to keep playing this from time to time.

The Game sounds and Looks amazing. 

The DLCs are mostly cosmetic in Nature, except for the Pathogen one. I do not own it yet, since it only offers a single new campaign with a playtime of rougly 1 hours. Maybe I´ll grab it once its on sale for 5€.

TL;DR:
If you´re a Diehard alien fan, buy it. If you´re looking for solid Coop fun. Buy it. 

Thanks for Reading.
